identity: The common twelve-point construction was compared across the Boston 1889, ATF 1896, GPO 1897, census 1900, job-room 1904 and document 1904 specimens. Comparisons with the 33 existing text families found no identical revival. The Celtic No. 2 capitals are narrower and have different figures. Other labelled point sizes require separate optical comparison.

rejected_sources.reason: Native pixel dimensions are larger, but the impression is substantially heavier and more rounded; comparison and naming provenance only.
Useful earlier named twelve-point witness; matching characters are softer/smaller than preferred census or job-room impressions.
Attached stray ink midway along stem; use complete matching job-room L.

rejected_sources.reason: Weak central join drops half the drawing at lower thresholds. A later w in will is complete without increasing the whole letter weight.

rejected_trials.reason: Initial thresholds of 200 for the census and 180 for the 1897 source capture too much scan fringe and thicken the light cut.

Thresholds of 110–130 can remove hairline connections and entire components. A job-room threshold of 155 loses n, r and q connections; 170 preserves the complete forms. Q at 150 opens the small tail loop; 170 retains it.

geometry: Rigid row rotations from measured cap/baseline lines; one physical scale per source page. Lowercase and punctuation inherit that page scale, preserving observed size and vertical placement. No independent horizontal stretch or fitted analytic repairs.
visual_review: All 66 visible forms were inspected against native crops at 170 and 32 pixels; words were reviewed at 16, 24, 40, 64 and 96 pixels. Q has two observed enclosed spaces; i and j retain detached dots. Counter counts supplement visual inspection and cannot detect a missing disconnected half of n, r or w.
